prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Sign-in reordering (sign_in, reorder) is helpful, averaging +3.0% after noise correction across 3 tests with 2 winning tests, though 1 test showed no clear effect.
Evidence is still thin for adding new adoption screens (adoption, new_screen) with only 1 test, which showed no clear effect.
Evidence is still thin for path choice redesigns (choose_path, redesign) with only 1 test, which showed no clear effect.
Evidence is still thin for finish redesigns (finish, redesign) with only 1 test, despite it winning.
Predictions are often too high, overestimating actual noise-corrected impact in most tests.
Predictions can sometimes underestimate actual impact, as in round 6 (+1.5% predicted vs +3.1% noise-corrected) and round 7 (+2.2% predicted vs +4.6% noise-corrected).

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_screen: +0.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, redesign: +1.0% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, redesign: +3.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: +3.0% after noise correction, 3 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 81.5%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 71.0%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 21.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [finish, redesign] Two column home intro overview: Redesign the home intro finish screen into a clear two-column layout highlighting essential pet controls and desktop shortcuts. (why: 29% drop-off at finish screen (mean time 5815s) and support emails show confusion on how to control or hide pets.)
1: [home, wait_info] Generation progress timer and tips: Add a visual completion timer and tip carousel component to the waiting screen while pet assets generate. (why: Home waiting screen has high mean wait duration (2336s) causing users to assume the app stalled.)
2: [sign_in, copy] Account pet recovery explicit reassurance: Update sign-in headline and body text to clearly explain that signing in saves and secures pet data across reinstalls. (why: 8 support emails complained about pets missing or resetting after signing in again.)
3: [choose_path, layout] Story scroll intro layout: Change the story screen layout to story_scroll for an engaging visual intro before choosing a creation path. (why: 76.2% conversion on path selection leaves room for improvement by visually framing expectations early.)
4: [finish, notification] Desktop updates ready notification: Enable optional desktop notifications on the final home intro screen to keep users informed when features update. (why: 4 support emails reported desktop feature misbehavior post-setup; notifications help communicate fixes and tips.)

scores.note: Target screen has largest drop-off and support mail alignment; finish redesign previously won (+3.1%).
High mean wait duration on home screen indicates perceived stall, but requires new components.
8 support emails directly target pet loss fears; copy-only change on a reliable step.
Low evidence without support complaints; past choose_path redesign showed no clear effect.
Addresses post-setup support emails, but notification opt-in has minor impact on step conversion.
